incoming.explanation: Manuscript grants evidence John's inhabitant standing at Weymouth.
The 1636 great-lot absence refines the start of John's inhabitant standing: he was not yet a Weymouth householder in 1636, so his admitted-inhabitant window opens after 1636.

Distinguishes John's residence-era inhabitant standing (early 1640s) from the later 1651-52 proprietary right, which is not evidence of residence - guarding the standing finding against over-reading the great lot.
That John's land-neighbours were an established Aylesbury-Vale regional cluster frames his grants as reception into a settled community, reinforcing the admitted-inhabitant reading.
Uses the inhabitant-standing finding to connect the later grants with residence at Weymouth.
Uses John's early Weymouth residence as context for the possible debt period.

outgoing.explanation: John's original Weymouth grants support the arrival range by showing later residence there.

finding.statement: John Gurney was an admitted, resident inhabitant of Weymouth c. 1638/9-c. 1642/4: early-Massachusetts town land divisions went only to admitted inhabitants, so his three original East/Mill-Field grants mark him as a recognised member of the Weymouth community before his removal to Braintree.

incoming.explanation: Uses the original Weymouth grants as evidence of John's later settled presence there.

outgoing.explanation: The manuscript Land Grants book supports the arrival range by documenting John's original Weymouth grants.

finding.shortLabel: Manuscript Land Grants book: John original grantee of 3 parcels
finding.statement: The Weymouth proprietors' manuscript Land Grants book records John Gurney as original grantee of three parcels - two East Field lots (ms pp. 12, 23, under Robert Randoll and Nathaniel Addames) and one Mill Field lot (ms p. 31, under Thomas Richardes), about eight acres in all - each 'first granted/given to John Gurny/Gurnie.'
